title: BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook.pull() allows fully-accrued debt to be redirected to a new recipient set immediately before the call
description:
`pull()` mints the full accumulated `mintDebt` to whatever address is currently stored in `recipient`. `setRecipient(newRecipient)` is unrestricted (aside from `onlyOwner`) and has no timelock, no cap, and no snapshot of the debt at time of configuration. The natural reading of the hook's docstring is that `recipient` is the beneficiary of the `ratio%` mint-debt stream generated by historical dispatches — but the contract's semantics are 'whoever is recipient at the moment pull() fires gets 100% of the ledger'.

Concrete failure path: debt accrues for months under `recipient = A`. Owner mistakenly (or maliciously — but owner-driven attacks are OOS; relevant path here is accidental misconfig + griefing by front-runner) calls `setRecipient(B)`. An attacker observes the `RecipientUpdated` event or the mempool tx, front-runs by calling `pull()` immediately after the setRecipient is mined (or sandwiches the setRecipient with two pull()s if A is the attacker). Either way, the recipient at the instant of pull() collects the entire accrued ledger — debts that morally belonged to A on the protocol's accounting side are paid to B.

Because `pull()` is callable by `owner || recipient`, either A or B can race the owner's setRecipient call: A can call pull() right before setRecipient lands; B can call pull() right after. There is no atomic mechanism to 'snapshot at set-time and let old recipient pull the old balance'.
impact: Accrued phUSD mint-debt can be redirected wholesale from the intended beneficiary to a successor beneficiary (or vice versa) by a single owner call, with no way to carve off pre-existing debt. Any dispute between recipients or any operational error on `setRecipient` timing can cause material amounts of phUSD to materialise in the wrong address. Because recipients here are likely treasury/multisig addresses, the ordering risk is a present-day operational attack surface rather than a pure owner-trust issue.
attack_path: Owner previously called setRecipient(A); mintDebt has accrued to D over many dispatches.
Owner signs tx to setRecipient(B) (e.g. rotating treasury signers).
A (or B, depending on who acts first) front-runs in the same block: A calls pull() before setRecipient executes → A collects D; or B calls pull() right after → B collects D.
There is no mechanism to split the ledger; whichever ordering wins, one party collects the full historic balance.
recommendation: Either (a) require `mintDebt == 0` as a precondition of `setRecipient` (forces owner to call `pull()` for the old recipient before changing it), or (b) snapshot: on `setRecipient(newRecipient)` auto-settle the outstanding debt to the old recipient (call into the pull path) atomically in the same function, or (c) maintain per-recipient debt ledgers keyed by address so each recipient is only ever paid what was accrued under their tenure.
